relationships.subject: common peroneal nerve ligation
relationships.evidence_quote: DSI amplitude was significantly increased in RAIC layer V pyramidal neurons after CPN ligation, while DSE was not changed.

relationships.subject: AM251
relationships.evidence_quote: The DSI was blocked by AM251

relationships.subject: AM251
relationships.evidence_quote: the strong analgesia induced by CB1R activation in the RAIC was reversed by the CB1R antagonist AM251

relationships.subject: CB1R
relationships.evidence_quote: The analgesia of CB1R activation required CB1Rs in GABAergic neurons of the RAIC as well following CPN ligation, but not in glutamatergic neurons.

relationships.subject: CB1R
relationships.evidence_quote: The CB1R activation-mediated analgesic effect in the RAIC was alleviated following a DLF lesion demonstrating that antinociception develops via the descending pain inhibitory pathway.

relationships.subject: common peroneal nerve ligation
relationships.evidence_quote: The E/I ratio (amplitude ratio between mEPSCs and mIPSCs) was significantly increased in layer V pyramidal neurons of the RAIC in CPN-ligated mice.

key_findings: CPN ligation increases the E/I ratio and CB1R-dependent DSI (but not DSE) in RAIC layer V pyramidal neurons.
Analgesia by the CB1R agonist ACEA in RAIC requires CB1R in GABAergic (not glutamatergic) neurons and depends on the dorsolateral funiculus descending pathway.
